title: Tombstone Protocol v1
description: The redacted fatal-error payload emitted by a crash guard (packages/fatal-guard) and consumed by scripts/tombstone_to_draft.py and scripts/fatal_guard_handler.py. Machine-readable form of docs/tombstone-protocol.md § v1. Required fields are the ones the consumer needs to produce a draft; everything else is enrichment. Additional properties are allowed on purpose: the protocol grows additively and a reader must ignore fields it does not know.

schemaVersion.description: Payload shape version. Optional because the Python sidecar predates the field; when present it must be 1 (v2 is a draft and is not emitted by the reference implementation).

reason.description: Why the process ended. killed_by_<SIGNAL> carries the signal name.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time the crash was observed. The pattern is redundant with format for tools without a format checker; both say the same thing.

pid.description: Process id of the crashed process.

message.description: Redacted error message. The Node wrapper truncates to 500 chars.

stackSnippet.description: Redacted stack excerpt. The Node wrapper truncates to 1000 chars.

snippet.description: Error text as the Python sidecar writes it; the consumer accepts snippet or message+stackSnippet.

exit_code.description: Process exit code when the crash was an exit (Node wrapper).

exitCode.description: v2 draft spelling; accepted so a v2-shaped payload from an older guard still validates.

signal.description: Signal name when the process was killed (v2 draft; optional in v1).

host.description: Host label added by a sidecar that knows it; never required.

node_id.description: Anonymous node id, when the guard is registered.

tombstone_hash.description: Stable dedupe hash, when a consumer computed one.
